interface.name: maton_ahb_manager_v1

description.summary: private AHardwareBuffer transport, not Vulkan WSI

interface.description: Buffers use complete nativewindow handle serialization on a dedicated SOCK_SEQPACKET socket, never Wayland's byte stream or gralloc metadata. This protocol alone does not promise FIFO pacing or Vulkan image layouts.

interface.name: maton_ahb_session_v1

description.summary: one surface on the client's existing connection

interface.description: The server creates a socketpair and transfers one endpoint in transport. Only this session writes handles to its other endpoint. A client must receive exactly one AHardwareBuffer per allocated event, in event order, using AHardwareBuffer_recvHandleFromUnixSocket on resident bionic TLS. Client render work and external-memory ownership release MUST complete before wl_surface.commit. There is no implicit render synchronization. A buffer may be reused only after wl_buffer.release, including final SurfaceFlinger fence completion. Session destruction closes transport but existing wl_buffers keep their own storage until their final reader ends.

request.name: create_buffer
request.description: request is a client-chosen nonzero sequence, strictly increasing and never reused. A successful allocated event creates the wl_buffer; a failure creates no object. fd transfer can arrive before allocated. The handle socket is read-only to clients. No pointer crosses the wire.
